title: Class 6 Science · Ch 2 Worksheet B · Animals and Adaptations
instructions: Practise classifying animals and identifying their adaptations.

questions.question: Animals that eat both plants and other animals are called
questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals (e.g., humans, crows).

questions.question: Fish breathe with
questions.explanation: Gills extract dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.question: Which adaptation BEST helps a polar bear survive in the Arctic?
questions.explanation: Thick fur insulates against cold; white colour hides the bear in snow.

questions.question: An animal that lives both on land and in water is called an _____.
questions.explanation: Amphibians like frogs and salamanders live both on land and in water.

questions.question: A whale is a fish because it lives in water.
questions.explanation: Whales are mammals — they breathe air through lungs and feed milk to their young.

questions.question: Mention any two adaptations a camel has for desert life.
questions.answer: A hump that stores fat for energy and water; long legs that keep its body away from hot sand; ability to drink large amounts of water at once and conserve it for days. Any two are correct.

questions.question: Compare a fish and a frog: how are their adaptations different even though both spend time in water?
questions.answer: A fish has gills (only) and a streamlined body; it must stay in water. A frog has lungs and skin to breathe; webbed feet for swimming and jumping legs for land. The frog can leave the water; the fish cannot.
questions.explanation: Tests comparing aquatic vs amphibian adaptations.

questions.question: Design a simple key (yes/no questions) to identify these animals: cow, eagle, fish, lizard.
questions.answer: Sample key. Q1: Does the animal live mostly in water? Yes -> Fish. No -> Q2. Q2: Does it have feathers? Yes -> Eagle. No -> Q3. Q3: Does it have hair/fur and feed milk to young? Yes -> Cow. No -> Lizard. (Other valid yes/no chains also accepted.)
